chunks: And in the narration of Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

He was asked about what the mi'rad strikes down from game, so he said: “If he has no arrows other than the mi'rad, and he mentions the Name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, over it, then let him eat from what it killed. But if he has arrows other than it, then no.”

key_terms.اسْمَ اللَّهِ: the Name of Allah invoked at the time of hunting
key_terms.الْمِعْرَاضُ: a hunting implement used to strike game

ai.seo_question: Is game killed by a mi'rad halal to eat in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on hunted game killed by a mi'rad. It permits eating such game when no other arrow is available and Allah's Name is mentioned, but forbids it when other arrows are available.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4133 - In a narration from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (as):

Imam (as) was asked about what the 'mi'raad' (a hunting tool) strikes down from game.
Imam (as) said: "If he has no other arrows except the 'Mi'rad' and mentioned the name of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, over it, then he may eat from what it killed. However, if he had other arrows besides it, then he should not."
